resources.string: A crop writes only the centre of the sensor: the same readout, a narrower field of view.
No configuration is qualified on this camera yet.
It takes several minutes, and the camera is unavailable meanwhile.

RAW video writes every frame uncompressed to Documents/OpenCineCam/RAW. Only the sizes and frame rates this phone has qualified on its storage are offered: each one passed a long storage test and a live take without losing a frame. Automatic picks the highest qualified rate. A crop keeps the full sensor readout but writes only its centre, so the picture is narrower. The time shown is how long the free storage lasts at that rate.
An OpenCine RAW take. The player shows a developed preview; for full quality, copy or share it to a computer and convert it with the desktop DNG converter.
Risky rate: possible micro-stutters, latency or a corrupted file
The warning sign marks a risky rate: the storage is too slow for it, so a take may stutter, lag or end up corrupted. Automatic never picks one.
Risky rate: frames may drop after about %1$s (with a rested phone)

Applies to compressed configurations. Lossless keeps every value the sensor delivered. Near-lossless merges values that differ by less than about half the sensor noise at the frame’s ISO, so the difference stays hidden in the noise and files shrink further, most in low light. Both open in the gallery, the CinemaDNG export and the desktop tools. The time left assumes the same conservative ratio for both.
